description: Add an animated battle sequence to the wild-monster battle (issue #9). Today the battle result is shown all at once with a static log and no motion. Replace this with a turn-by-turn animated playback: both combatants shown with HP bars, per-turn attack motion (attacker lunge/shake, defender hit flash+shake), a damage-number popup, HP bars tweening down smoothly, and the battle log revealed one line at a time in sync. The localized winner headline (winnerLabelJa) appears at the end. Depends on FEAT-001 (green baseline). The testable core is a NEW pure parser added to ui-helpers.ts that converts the structured `log: string[]` into an ordered list of turn events; the UI is driven off that parser.
steps: In packages/frontend/src/ui-helpers.ts, add a pure, React-free parser. Define an exported type BattleTurnEvent = { turn: number; attacker: 'player' | 'enemy'; defender: 'player' | 'enemy'; dmg: number; defenderHpAfter: number } and an exported type BattlePlayback = { events: BattleTurnEvent[]; winner: BattleWinner | null }. Add `export function parseBattleEvents(log: readonly string[]): BattlePlayback`.

Implement parseBattleEvents by REUSING the existing TURN_LINE_RE and RESULT_LINE_RE regexes (do not invent new formats). For each matching turn line, map the captured HP-side token to attacker/defender: the regex capture group `side` is the side whose HP REMAINS after the hit, i.e. the DEFENDER. So side==='enemy' means the player attacked the enemy -> attacker:'player', defender:'enemy', defenderHpAfter:hp; side==='player' means the enemy attacked -> attacker:'enemy', defender:'player', defenderHpAfter:hp. Parse turn number and dmg as integers. For the result line, set winner. Unknown/unmatched lines are ignored gracefully (skipped, never throw). If no result line is present, winner stays null.

Add tests in packages/frontend/src/game-ui.test.ts for parseBattleEvents, keeping the file DOM/React-free. Cover: a player-attack line maps to attacker 'player'/defender 'enemy' with correct dmg and defenderHpAfter; an enemy-attack line maps to attacker 'enemy'/defender 'player'; a full multi-turn log plus `Result: player` yields the right ordered events and winner; unknown lines are ignored (e.g. a stray 'something unexpected' between turns does not appear and does not throw); an empty log yields { events: [], winner: null }; a log with turns but no Result line yields winner null. Use the exact line format from battle.ts, e.g. 'T1: でじたん hits 野生の幼年期モンスター for 11 (enemy HP 7)' and 'T2: 野生の幼年期モンスター hits でじたん for 2 (player HP 18)'.

Rewrite packages/frontend/src/components/BattlePanel.tsx into an animated panel. Accept the player's starting HP context so HP bars can be drawn. Add props so BattlePanel can derive both combatants' max/start HP: pass the player's stats and stageId from App.tsx. Recommended prop shape: keep existing { busy, log, result, onBattle } and ADD `playerName: string`, `playerStageId: GrowthStage`, `playerMaxHp: number`, `playerStartHp: number`. The enemy mirrors the backend: name `野生の${stageLabelJa(playerStageId)}モンスター`? NOTE the backend uses the shared stage labelJa which equals stageLabelJa already in ui-helpers; enemy stageId === player stageId; enemy maxHp = Math.round(getStage(playerStageId).baseStats.maxHp * 0.9). Import getStage from @ddm/shared (already a dependency) OR, to avoid importing shared into the component, derive enemy max HP from the first observed 'enemy HP' event instead (documented fallback). Keep it simple and document whichever approach is chosen in a code comment.

In BattlePanel, when a new result arrives (detect via a changing result/log identity), run parseBattleEvents(log) and step through events on a timer at ~800ms per event using setInterval or chained setTimeout. On each step: set the current attacker/defender motion classes, show a damage popup over the defender with the dmg number, and update the defender's displayed HP to event.defenderHpAfter (CSS transition on the bar width makes it tween smoothly). Append the localized log line (battleLogLineJa) for that event so the log grows one line at a time. After the last event, reveal the localized winner line (winnerLabelJa(result.winner)). Player starting HP for the bar = playerStartHp (the pre-battle HP) and enemy starting HP = enemy max HP; decrement each via the parsed defenderHpAfter values.

Make replay clean: pressing the battle button again must restart the animation from turn 1 with fresh HP bars and an empty revealed log. Reset all animation state when a new battle result is detected. Clear any interval/timeout on unmount and before starting a new run (follow the timer-cleanup pattern used in App.tsx for care FX). Do not freeze the UI: the battle() call already resolves immediately with the full result, so the animation is purely presentational on top of state that is already settled.

Render both combatants in BattlePanel using MonsterSprite (import from ../assets/monsters/MonsterSprite.tsx) at a smaller size (e.g. size=96 or 110): the player on one side, the enemy '野生の...モンスター' on the other, each with a name label and an HP bar (reuse hpPercent from ui-helpers for bar width). Apply attacker/defender animation classes per the current step. Keep the existing battle button and the final winner headline.

Add battle animation CSS to packages/frontend/src/styles.css near the existing `--- battle ---` section (~line 461). Add: a .battle-stage fl/flex layout for the two combatants, HP bar styles with a width transition (e.g. transition: width 500ms ease), @keyframes for an attacker lunge (translateX toward the opponent) and a defender hit (shake + flash/filter), a .damage-pop popup keyframe (rise + fade), and classes to toggle these per combatant/side. Add a prefers-reduced-motion @media block (mirror the one at ~line 269) that disables the lunge/shake/popup motion while still revealing the final state (HP bars jump to final, full log shown, winner shown).

Update packages/frontend/src/App.tsx to pass the new BattlePanel props from game.monster: playerName={game.monster.name}, playerStageId={game.monster.stageId}, playerMaxHp={game.monster.stats.maxHp}, and the pre-battle HP for playerStartHp. IMPORTANT: useMonster.battle() commits the UPDATED (post-battle) monster, so game.monster.stats.hp is already the end HP by the time the result is set; capture the player's starting HP for the bar from the FIRST 'player HP' decrement baseline instead, or compute player start HP as playerMaxHp (full) if a reliable pre-battle value is not available. Choose the simplest correct approach and document it: deriving the player's start HP as playerMaxHp is acceptable since battles begin from a revived/full-ish state; the parsed defenderHpAfter values then drive the bar down to the real end HP. Ensure the enemy bar starts at enemy max HP.
Keep all UI strings Japanese (no i18n framework; that is issue #12). Reuse existing helpers: battleLogLineJa, winnerLabelJa, hpPercent, stageLabelJa.
acceptance_criteria: `npm test -w @ddm/frontend` passes, including the new parseBattleEvents tests, with no regressions to the existing 17 tests.

parseBattleEvents is pure (no DOM/React), reuses the existing TURN_LINE_RE/RESULT_LINE_RE patterns, maps the HP-side token to the correct attacker/defender, ignores unknown lines without throwing, and returns winner null when no Result line is present.
`npm run build` compiles the whole monorepo with no TypeScript errors (BattlePanel prop changes wired through App.tsx).

BattlePanel renders two combatants with HP bars, plays turn-by-turn attack motion with damage popups, tweens HP bars down to the parsed defenderHpAfter values, reveals the log one line at a time, and shows the localized winner at the end.
Pressing the battle button again cleanly restarts the animation; timers are cleared on unmount and before a new run (no leaked intervals/timeouts).
A prefers-reduced-motion @media block exists that disables lunge/shake/popup motion while still showing the final HP, full log, and winner.
findings:
Implemented the animated battle sequence (issue #9). Changes:
- ui-helpers.ts: added pure React-free parser `parseBattleEvents(log): BattlePlayback` plus exported types BattleTurnEvent and BattlePlayback. Reuses existing TURN_LINE_RE/RESULT_LINE_RE; maps the HP-side token to attacker/defender (side==='enemy' => player attacked enemy; side==='player' => enemy attacked player), parses turn/dmg/hp as ints, skips unknown lines without throwing, winner null when no Result line.
- game-ui.test.ts: added 6 tests for parseBattleEvents (player-attack mapping, enemy-attack mapping, full multi-turn log + winner, unknown-line skip, empty log, no-Result winner null). Kept DOM/React-free.
- BattlePanel.tsx: rewritten into an animated panel. New props playerName, playerStageId, playerMaxHp, playerStartHp. Renders both combatants via MonsterSprite (player size 110, enemy 96, enemy mirrored). Enemy derived to mirror backend: name `野生の${stageLabelJa(stageId)}モンスター`, maxHp = round(getStage(stageId).baseStats.maxHp*0.9) (getStage imported from @ddm/shared). Steps through parseBattleEvents on a setInterval at 800ms/turn: sets attacker/defender motion classes, shows a damage popup over the defender, updates defender HP (CSS width transition tweens the bar), appends one localized log line (battleLogLineJa) per turn, then reveals winnerLabelJa. Timer cleared on unmount and before each new run; a changing log identity restarts cleanly from turn 1 with fresh HP bars and empty log.
- App.tsx: passes new props from game.monster. playerStartHp = game.monster.stats.maxHp (full) with a documenting comment, because useMonster.battle() commits the post-battle monster so stats.hp is already the END hp; parsed defenderHpAfter values drive the bar down.
- styles.css: added .battle-stage flex layout, HP bar styles with `transition: width 500ms ease`, lunge/hit keyframes (with mirrored variants for the flipped enemy), a .damage-pop rise+fade keyframe, and a prefers-reduced-motion @media block that disables lunge/shake/popup motion and the bar transition while still showing final HP, full log, and winner. No new runtime dependencies.

Verification (repo root): `npm run build` -> exit 0, all four workspaces compile, vite built (51 modules). `npm test` (shared) -> 47/47 pass. `npm test -w @ddm/frontend` -> 23/23 pass (17 baseline + 6 new). Note: package-lock.json has an unrelated one-line `dev: true` normalization from FEAT-001's npm install; left unstaged, not part of this commit.
